subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw core own an automated same-product archive import/restore command, or should core instead keep restore user-driven and add safer backup export/convert/platform-targeting support?
rationale: The answer determines the permanent CLI namespace, destructive write policy, archive trust model, secret/session portability rules, and whether overlapping backup and migration PRs should proceed in core.

options.title: Prefer backup export/convert first
options.body: Keep restore user-driven for now, improve backup platform targeting/conversion and manual restore docs, and avoid a broad destructive importer until a security design is sponsored.

options.title: Approve a native import contract
options.body: Sponsor a preview-first core import/export lifecycle with canonical target validation, archive trust checks, rollback/conflict handling, secret/session policy, and focused security tests.

options.title: Push optional scope to plugins
options.body: Limit core to missing migration/backup APIs and let plugin or ClawHub packages own optional cloud, encrypted, scheduled, or workspace-specific migration flows.

recommendation.title: Prefer backup export/convert first
recommendation.body: Keep restore user-driven for now, improve backup platform targeting/conversion and manual restore docs, and avoid a broad destructive importer until a security design is sponsored.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior implementation discussion already centered on this person's restore security-boundary objection and alternative backup-convert direction.
